newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: No need for Bundesbank to change rates now - Gaddum.
newsitem.headline: No need for Bundesbank to change rates now - Gaddum.

text.p: Bundesbank Vice President Johann Wilhelm Gaddum said the German central bank was able to act on the interest rate front but saw no need to do so at this time.
"Concerning interest rates, the Bundesbank is able to act but does not see any need to act at this time," Gaddum told Reuters while attending the World Economic Forum in Davos.
"Monetary policy is expansive and capital market interest rates are at lows. There is no need to act in terms of interest rate policy," Gaddum said.

He said the Bundesbank's most important contribution to growth was ensuring that companies and markets maintain their expectations for low inflation and capital market interest rates as long as possible.
"We will achieve this by making clear that the Bundesbank remains fully able to act on interest rates until the end of 1998," he said.
